chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever sees his brother engaged in something he disapproves of and does not turn him away from it while he is able to do so, then he has betrayed him.
And whoever does not avoid befriending a fool is close to adopting his character.

key_terms.الأحمق: The fool - one lacking wisdom and sound judgment, whose company corrupts character
key_terms.خانه: Betrayed him - khiyanah (betrayal) is a serious moral failing in Islamic ethics, here applied to neglect of communal duty
key_terms.مصادقة: Befriending, forming close friendship - implies deep, intimate companionship rather than casual acquaintance
key_terms.يتخلق بأخلاقه: Adopt his character/morals - the principle that companionship shapes moral disposition

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about correcting your brother and avoiding friendship with fools?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches two interconnected ethical principles in this hadith. First, that neglecting to correct a brother's wrongdoing when one is able constitutes a form of betrayal, reflecting the Islamic duty of mutual accountability (nasiha). Second, that associating with fools inevitably leads to moral corruption, since companionship shapes one's character. This teaching was delivered in the context of the close-knit Muslim community of Kufa and Medina, where the concept of religious brotherhood (ukhuwwa) carried deep obligations.
